'''Randy Villegas''' (born November 12, 1994) is an American professor, businessman, and politician. Villegas is the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in California (districts 1–26)#District 22|2026 election]] for [[California's 22nd congressional district]], which encompasses the southern [[Central Valley (California)|Central Valley]]. In California's June 2026 top-two primary, he finished ahead of Democratic state assemblymember [[Jasmeet Bains]] and advanced to the general election against Republican incumbent [[David Valadao]]. Villegas works as a professor at the [[College of the Sequoias]].

== Early life and education ==
Villegas was born and raised in [[Bakersfield, California]] in California's [[Central Valley (California)|Central Valley]]. His parents were working-class [[Mexican-Americans|Mexican immigrants]].<ref name=NBC2026Wading /><ref name=EFE2026Mecanico /> His father, a mechanic, was born in [[Michoacán]] and his mother in [[Guerrero]].<ref name="Fresnoland2026Weaver" /><ref name=LaOpinion2026Avanza>{{cite news |last=Roura |first=Ricardo |title=Randy Villegas avanza a elecciones generales del distrito 22 de California |url=https://laopinion.com/2026/06/09/randy-villegas-avanza-a-elecciones-generales-del-distrito-22-de-california/ |work=La Opinión |date=June 9, 2026 |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260610084703/https://laopinion.com/2026/06/09/randy-villegas-avanza-a-elecciones-generales-del-distrito-22-de-california/ |archive-date=June 10, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> While Villegas was born a United States citizen, his older brother Angel was undocumented and later received protection under [[Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals]] (DACA) in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=Divided By Immigration Status: Brothers Reflect On Their Bond |url=https://storycorps.org/stories/divided-by-immigration-status-brothers-reflect-on-their-bond/ |website=StoryCorps |date=April 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423142422/https://storycorps.org/stories/divided-by-immigration-status-brothers-reflect-on-their-bond/ |archive-date=April 23, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=LATimes2026ICE /> During his childhood, the family received [[Medicaid]] and [[Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program]] support during his childhood.<ref name=NBC2026Wading /> Villegas attended [[Golden Valley High School (Bakersfield, California)|Golden Valley High School]], where he played in the [[Marching percussion|drumline]].<ref name="KGET2026Demonte">{{cite news |last=Demonte |first=Vincent |title=The race for District 22: A one-on-one with Randy Villegas |url=https://www.kget.com/news/politics/your-local-elections/the-race-for-district-22-a-one-on-one-with-randy-villegas/ |work=[[KGET-TV|KGET 17 News]] |date=May 6, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507184715/https://www.kget.com/news/politics/your-local-elections/the-race-for-district-22-a-one-on-one-with-randy-villegas/ |archive-date=May 7, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="APSA" />

Villegas was the first member of his family to graduate from college.<ref name="SouthKern">{{cite news |title=From first-gen student to Congressional candidate: Randy Villegas aims to uplift the valley |url=https://southkernsol.org/2025/04/21/from-first-gen-student-to-congressional-candidate-randy-villegas-aims-to-uplift-the-valley/ |work=South Kern Sol |date=April 21, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250524034206/https://southkernsol.org/2025/04/21/from-first-gen-student-to-congressional-candidate-randy-villegas-aims-to-uplift-the-valley/ |archive-date=May 24, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> He earned an associate degree in political science from [[Bakersfield College]] and a bachelor's degree from [[California State University, Bakersfield]]. He subsequently earned a master's degree in political science and a Ph.D. in politics from the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] on a full-ride fellowship.<ref name="KGET2025Huh">{{cite news |last=Huh |first=Jenny |title=Meet Kern's 2026 primary candidates: One-on-one interview with CD-22 hopeful Randy Villegas |url=https://www.kget.com/news/politics/your-local-elections/meet-kerns-2026-primary-candidates-one-on-one-interview-with-cd-22-hopeful-randy-villegas/ |work=[[KGET-TV|KGET 17 News]] |date=April 14, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416011429/https://www.kget.com/news/politics/your-local-elections/meet-kerns-2026-primary-candidates-one-on-one-interview-with-cd-22-hopeful-randy-villegas/ |archive-date=April 16, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="APSA" /><ref name="COSCatalog">{{cite web |title=Administration and Faculty |url=https://catalog.cos.edu/about-college-sequoias/directory/ |website=College of the Sequoias Academic Catalog |publisher=[[College of the Sequoias]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240912050125/https://catalog.cos.edu/about-college-sequoias/directory/ |archive-date=September 12, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> Villegas completed his doctorate in 2022.<ref name="Dissertation">{{cite thesis |last=Villegas |first=Randy |title=Voices from the Valley of Vulnerability |degree=Ph.D. in Politics, with an emphasis in Latin American and Latino Studies |publisher=[[University of California, Santa Cruz]] |date=2022 |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/6b67z1t1}}</ref>

== Career ==
Before attending graduate school, Villegas worked as a journalist and community organizer in Bakersfield. His writing appeared in English-language papers ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', ''[[The Bakersfield Californian]]'', ''South Kern Sol'', and the Spanish-language paper ''El Popular''.<ref name="APSA" />

Villegas is a professor of political science at the [[College of the Sequoias]] in [[Visalia, California]].<ref name="APSA">{{cite web |title=Randy Villegas Receives the 2025 APSA Community College Faculty Award |url=https://politicalsciencenow.com/randy-villegas-receives-the-2025-apsa-community-college-faculty-award/ |website=Political Science Now |publisher=[[American Political Science Association]] |date=August 13, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250814104014/https://politicalsciencenow.com/randy-villegas-receives-the-2025-apsa-community-college-faculty-award/ |archive-date=August 14, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2025, the [[American Political Science Association]] gave Villegas its Community College Faculty Award.<ref name="APSA" />

Villegas co-owns and helps operate his family's [[Automobile repair shop|auto body shop]].<ref name=WaPo2026MericaNovel /><ref name=Bloomberg2026Reframe>{{cite news |last=Sheehey |first=Maeve |title=California’s New House Map Reframes the Fight for GOP Incumbents |url=https://news.bloomberglaw.com/bloomberg-government-news/californias-new-house-map-reframes-the-fight-for-gop-incumbents |work=Bloomberg Government |date=August 28, 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20261003025025/https://news.bloomberglaw.com/bloomberg-government-news/californias-new-house-map-reframes-the-fight-for-gop-incumbents |archive-date=October 3, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=EFE2026Mecanico>{{cite news |last=Varón |first=Ana Milena |title=Randy Villegas, el mecánico y educador aspirante a un escaño del Congreso de EE.UU. |url=https://efe.com/mundo/2026-05-22/randy-villegas-congreso-eeuu/ |work=EFE |date=May 22, 2026 |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260522120216/https://efe.com/mundo/2026-05-22/randy-villegas-congreso-eeuu/ |archive-date=May 22, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Political career ==

=== Visalia school board ===
In December 2021, the Visalia Unified School District Board of Education appointed Villegas to fill a vacancy representing Trustee Area 6.<ref name="ValleyVoiceAppointment">{{cite news |title=Visalia Unified School District Board Provisionally Appoints Randy Villegas to Trustee Area 6 Seat |url=https://www.ourvalleyvoice.com/2021/12/10/visalia-unified-school-district-board-provisionally-appoints-randy-villegas-to-trustee-area-6-seat/ |work=Valley Voice |date=December 10, 2021}}</ref> In November 2022, Villegas was elected to a full term.<ref name="RedwoodElection">{{cite news |title=VUSD Board Elections 2022: Dr. Randy Villegas Elected to Trustee Area 6 Seat |url=https://redwoodgigantea.com/vusd-board-elections-2022-dr-randy-villegas-elected-to-trustee-area-6-seat/ |work=Redwood Gigantea |date=February 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250316104041/https://redwoodgigantea.com/vusd-board-elections-2022-dr-randy-villegas-elected-to-trustee-area-6-seat/ |archive-date=March 16, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2026 congressional campaign ===
In 2025, Villegas announced his candidacy in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in California#District 22|2026 election]] for [[California's 22nd congressional district]], which encompasses the southern [[Central Valley (California)|Central Valley]]. news |last=Parsley |first=Haley |title=DCCC backs progressive Randy Villegas for Congress following Bains’ defeat |url=https://www.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article316082675.html |newspaper=The Sacramento Bee |date=June 12, 2026 name=Bloomberg2026Reframe /><ref name=Prospect2026Valley>{{cite news |last=Janssen |first=Emma |title=How Do You Beat a Central Valley Republican? == Political positions ==
Villegas is a [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]]<ref name="CalMattersPrimary" /><ref name="APGeneral" /><ref name=WaPo2026MericaNovel>{{cite news |last=Merica |first=Dan |title=Democrats try a novel path to defeat a battleground Republican: Moving to the left |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/09/07/california-progressive-tries-novel-path-fight-against-gop-swing-district/ |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=September 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20260907125748/https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/09/07/california-progressive-tries-novel-path-fight-against-gop-swing-district/?outputType=amp |archive-date=September 7, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> whose campaign emphasizes economic populism and local issues.<ref name="CalMattersPrimary" /><ref name="APGeneral" /> Villegas supports [[universal healthcare]], expanding the [[right to organize]] for [[labor union]]s, increased funding for [[public education]], [[Immigration reform in the United States|immigration reform]], overturning ''[[Citizens United v. FEC]]'' and expanding public financing for elections.<ref name="CalMattersPrimary" />

=== Data centers ===
Villegas supports a one-year moratorium on new [[data center]] construction<ref>{{cite news |last=McDaniel |first=Justine |title=Backlash over data centers hits California, and the midterms |url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2026-09-06/backlash-over-data-centers-hits-california-midterms |work=Los Angeles Times |date=September 6, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260916070129/https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2026-09-06/backlash-over-data-centers-hits-california-midterms |archive-date=September 16, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Verano |first=Brenda Fernanda |title=Congressional candidate demands pause on Central Valley data center expansion |url=https://www.calonews.com/featured-topics/environmental/congressional-candidate-demands-pause-on-central-valley-data-center-expansion/article_80124433-d4ea-4bbc-a498-ea95eeb6d050.html |work=CALÓ News |date=August 28, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261003024931/https://www.calonews.com/featured-topics/environmental/congressional-candidate-demands-pause-on-central-valley-data-center-expansion/article_80124433-d4ea-4bbc-a498-ea95eeb6d050.html |archive-date=October 3, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> and argues that data centers should pay the full cost for their own electricity.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rangel |first=Samantha |title=Democratic House candidate in swing district calls for moratorium on data centers |url=https://www.kvpr.org/environment/2026-08-26/democratic-house-candidate-in-swing-district-calls-for-moratorium-on-data-centers |work=KVPR |date=August 26, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Miranda |first=Mathew |title=Fact Check: Where do David Valadao and Randy Villegas stand on data centers? |url=https://www.aol.com/articles/fact-check-where-david-valadao-183000000.html |newspaper=The Sacramento Bee |via=AOL |date=September 9, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260911203644/https://www.aol.com/articles/fact-check-where-david-valadao-183000000.html |archive-date=September 11, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Rangel |first=Samantha |title=Democratic House candidate Randy Villegas pitches himself to voters ahead of midterms |url=https://www.kvpr.org/government-politics/2026-08-21/democratic-house-candidate-randy-villegas-pitches-himself-to-voters-ahead-of-midterms |work=KVPR |date=August 21, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830192009/https://www.kvpr.org/government-politics/2026-08-21/democratic-house-candidate-randy-villegas-pitches-himself-to-voters-ahead-of-midterms |archive-date=August 30, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Healthcare ===
Villegas supports [[Medicare for All]], which is central to his platform.<ref name=Prospect2026Majority>{{cite news |last=Dayen |first=David |title=The New Majority Makers |url=https://prospect.org/2026/09/14/oct-2026-the-new-majority-makers/ |work=The American Prospect |date=September 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260914104709/https://prospect.org/2026/09/14/oct-2026-the-new-majority-makers/ |archive-date=September 14, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Alam |first=Christopher |title=Voters in This Competitive California District Say Healthcare Is the Key Issue |url=https://www.kqed.org/news/12097751/voters-in-this-competitive-california-district-say-healthcare-is-the-key-issue |work=KQED |date=September 1, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260903060020/https://www.kqed.org/news/12097751/voters-in-this-competitive-california-district-say-healthcare-is-the-key-issue |archive-date=September 3, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Villegas supports a reversal of the [[One Big Beautiful Bill Act]]'s cuts to [[Affordable Care Act]] healthcare subsidies.<ref name=Prospect2026Majority /><ref>{{cite news |last=Rangel |first=Samantha |title=In toss-up House district, voters crave leadership to fix broken healthcare |url=https://www.kvpr.org/health/2026-08-26/in-toss-up-house-district-voters-crave-leadership-to-fix-broken-healthcare |work=KVPR |date=August 26, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907030712/https://www.kvpr.org/health/2026-08-26/in-toss-up-house-district-voters-crave-leadership-to-fix-broken-healthcare |archive-date=September 7, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Villegas also supports price caps on prescription drugs and certain medical procedures.<ref name="CalMatters2026Strategy">{{cite news |last=Miller |first=Maya C. |title=‘Valleycrat’ or Mamdani wannabe?: California Democrats are split on how to win swing votes |url=https://calmatters.org/politics/2026/02/bains-villegas-democrats-central-valley/ |work=[[CalMatters]] |date=February 12, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260911095926/https://calmatters.org/politics/2026/02/bains-villegas-democrats-central-valley/ |archive-date=September 11, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Immigration ===
Villegas supports a [[Path to citizenship|pathway to citizenship]], banning [[List of immigrant detention sites in the United States|private detention facilities]], prosecuting unlawful [[Immigrations and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) conduct, and a secure border.<ref name=LATimes2026ICE>{{cite news |last=Castillo |first=Andrea |title=Trump supercharged ICE. Now battleground candidates are scrambling for a message |url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2026-09-27/trump-ice-battleground-candidates-message-midterms |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=September 27, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260927104934/https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2026-09-27/trump-ice-battleground-candidates-message-midterms |archive-date=September 27, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> He does not support abolishing ICE.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valdez |first=Jonah |date=2026-11-04 |title=In California’s Central Valley, ICE Swung a Red District Blue |url=https://theintercept.com/2026/11/04/villegas-valadao-california-election-ice/ |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=The Intercept |language=en-US}}</ref>
